documents.version: Rev 9/21 gdh. This is the file currently linked from the DHSR 'Requirements for Establishing a Home Care Agency' page.
documents.how_used: This is the primary document. DHSR tells applicants to use it as their guide. After DHSR receives the application and fee, it emails the applicant to request the policies, procedures and personnel documents. The initial survey then reviews them for compliance. Items below are listed as the checklist words them, with the rule cites printed on the form.

documents.title: 10A NCAC 13J .1001, .1003, .1004 (Licensing of Home Care Agencies, Subchapter 13J rules)
documents.issuer: NC Medical Care Commission, published by the NC Office of Administrative Hearings; enforced by DHSR
documents.version: Current codified text of Subchapter 13J. The .1001 history note shows it was found necessary without substantive public interest, eff. June 25, 2016. The .1004 history note shows it readopted eff. June 1, 2018.
documents.how_used: This is the regulation text behind the checklist's cites. Rule .1001(a) lists the written policies the governing body must establish. Items from this document are marked 'doc 1' below. I could not retrieve the text of rules .1007, .1101, .1107, .1110, .1111, .1202, .1401, .1402, .1503 or .1504 in full, so the sub-requirements of those rules are not listed beyond what the checklist itself states.

notes: DHSR has no separate policy-manual form. The Home Care Initial Survey Checklist (Rev 9/21) is the review tool. Submission process: (1) The applicant mails the license application (hcapp.pdf), the fee, and proof of prior home care ownership or of DHSR-approved home care training to DHSR, 2712 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-2712. (2) DHSR emails to confirm receipt, then emails a request for the policies, procedures and personnel documents. (3) The initial survey is a desk review of those documents against the licensure rules. If no further information is needed, DHSR emails an approval letter with instructions for printing the license from the Enterprise system. Organize the manual in the checklist's order and group it under its three policy headings: Administrative Policies, Client Care Policies and Personnel Policies. Label each policy with the rule cite printed on the checklist so the surveyor can check each line. The checklist does not number its items, so item_id values above are built from the section name and rule cite. Cites are as printed on the checklist, including its '.1001 (5)' for emergency preparedness (the rule text places it at .1001(a)(5)). Three checklist lines also cover the Supporting Documentation section. Only the Agency Organization Chart is policy content and appears in the items above. The other Supporting Documentation lines are excluded as non-policy paperwork: proof of prior ownership, the training certificate, the premises lease, articles of incorporation, and the annual projected budget. The checklist has no cite for the bloodborne pathogen and Hepatitis B policy lines. Rule .1003(f)(5)-(6) covers Hepatitis B and pathogen training records. The checklist marks some items 'if applicable' (Companion Sitter Agency Director) or ties them to a service type (companion/sitter rules .1503-.1504). For a Personal Home Care (in-home aide) agency, the in-home aide cites (.1107, .1110) apply. The Personnel Record Review grid is a record check, not policy content. It covers the application, resume, signed job description, license verification, NA registry and Health Care Personnel Registry check, competency verification, TB proof, bloodborne pathogen training proof, Hepatitis B proof, orientation, reference checks, and signed criminal background consent. The checklist page was last modified in 2018, but the checklist PDF itself is Rev 9/21. Confirm with DHSR (919-855-4620, DHSR.homecare@dhhs.nc.gov) that no newer revision exists before submitting.
